lessons_learned_iter8: The ``find_closest()`` global-argmin pattern is a textbook tracking bug on self-looping trajectories (helix, figure-8). Codex confirmed same pattern exists in scripts/benchmark.py:431 — should be ported there too.

After the monotonic-forward tracker fix, the parameter regime that previously tolerated helix_interior_inflate=1.08 no longer does. The tracker change alters which trajectory shapes are feasible; tuning from the false-positive era does not transfer.

ILC offsets from benchmark.py's kinematic sim do not transfer to PyBullet CF2X. The cross-track bias direction is apparently different. Porting ILC requires running it inside a PyBullet sim (much slower offline calibration).
``max_correction_m`` in compute_ilc_offset_table is a per-iteration clamp but the final cumulative offset can exceed it (observed: max_correction_m=0.15 → final max offset 0.225m).

``avg_tracking_error`` metric must gate on the ACTUAL target_source (trajectory vs gate_fallback), not on ``_ref_progress_time < total_time`` — otherwise the long helix-stall wall-clock time where drone is navigating via fallback but anchor hasn't reached total_time inflates the metric 4x.

Constrain polynomial velocity direction at helix waypoints to the racing tangent, preserving min-snap smoothness while forcing proper normal crossing.
Tested global PLAN_MAX_SPEED reductions — all crashed. A helix-only speed reduction (not touching the gate-6→gate-7 transition) might work. Would need per-segment profile override.
Codex flagged 2s search window may alias if drone jumps >2s forward. Not observed but adding a monotonicity-only fallback (no window limit) would eliminate the theoretical edge case.
